description: Reviewed, per-dataset locations of EEGLAB .fdt data files that do not sit beside their .set. Read by generate_zarr.py (load_fdt_declarations) on every run, for every dataset: a malformed file fails every conversion run, so it is loaded by a test in CI. Every entry is re-verified at conversion time against the .set header (nbchan x pnts x trials x 4 bytes), the target's exact byte size and its pinned annex_key, and any mismatch refuses that recording only (fdt_declaration_refused, not retried) while the rest of the dataset still serves. Add an entry only with byte-size evidence, never from a similar name alone. Operational limits: an incremental run does not rebuild a .set when this file or a .fdt under derivatives/ changes, because changes under derivatives/ never enter the worklist; only a --clean or --full run, or an engine version bump, reconverts it (the Hallu cron always passes --clean, so the next version change of the dataset does). Merging an entry does not retry recordings that already failed: requeue the dataset after deploy, e.g. hallu-zarr.sh --dataset <id> --requeue data_failed --execute (or --requeue done if other recordings converted).

on004306.note: Every raw .set embeds a .fdt name (subNN_sessN.fdt) that is absent beside it; the data files are under derivatives/fdt_files/ with inconsistent names. Each .set header was read from its annex object (SHA-256 checked against the key) and paired with the single .fdt whose byte size equals nbchan x pnts x trials x 4. The extension-less tmp* file in several folders is the same annex object as the .fdt beside it and is not used.
